Lazy-init guard for Julia setup

Source: R/ensure_julia.R
ensure_julia.Rd

Convenience wrapper for the common "call my package's setup_*() function the first time any Julia-using function is called" pattern. Idempotent: once state_env$ready is TRUE, this is a no-op.

Usage

ensure_julia(state_env, init_fn)

Arguments

state_env

An environment shared with julia_ready() used to track init state. The caller's R package typically owns this environment.

init_fn

A zero-argument function that performs the package's one-time setup (typically calling julia_ready() and julia_load_bridge()).

Value

Invisibly TRUE.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Inside the consuming package:
.my_pkg_env <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
setup_my_pkg <- function() {
  julia_ready(packages = "MyJuliaPkg", state_env = .my_pkg_env)
  julia_load_bridge("mypkg", "bridge.jl")
}
my_function <- function() {
  ensure_julia(.my_pkg_env, setup_my_pkg)
  call_julia("MyJuliaPkg.do_something")
}
} # }
